messages:
jenna_prodsec: Quick question — we're designing regional failover for Private deploys using AWS KMS multi-region keys (MRKs). If us-east-1 primary goes down and we failover to eu-west-1 replica, what's required to ensure ciphertext decryptability across accounts? @raj_infra any gotchas with cross-account grants?
raj_infra: Short answer: MRKs are fine but pay attention to which key was used to encrypt. A replica MRK has its own key id but supports Decrypt for ciphertexts created by other replicas if they're truly MRKs (same key material). You need to allow Decrypt on the replica key for the principal that originally encrypted, or use grants.
chris_sre: Follow-up: in cross-account case we usually create a role in the other account and add an explicit key policy or grant. Grants are easier for short-lived access. Remember grants are region-local so you need them on each replica.
jenna_prodsec: When key rotation happens in MRKs, does rotation replicate? Will old ciphertexts still decrypt?
raj_infra: MRK rotation: when you rotate primary, KMS rotates the primary's key material and can replicate to replicas depending on setup. But KMS MRKs preserve ability to decrypt older ciphertexts because ciphertexts include key metadata; rotation only affects future encrypts. Old ciphertexts remain decryptable as long as key state isn't disabled/deleted.
chris_sre: Important operational note: scheduled deletion or DisableKey affects all replicas? Deleting a replica doesn't delete others. But scheduling deletion of a primary doesn't auto-propagate — be careful. Always test key state transitions.
eva_security: For envelope encryption: recommend encrypting data key with MRK in same region as the data plane. Store encrypted DEK alongside object and prefer re-encrypting DEK during failover if needed.
jenna_prodsec: Any example IAM policy or grant snippet for cross-account decrypt on replica?
raj_infra: Example grant CLI: 
```
aws kms create-grant --key-id arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:111122223333:key/abcd-... \
 --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::444455556666:role/PrivateDataPlaneRole \
 --operations Decrypt,ReEncryptFrom,ReEncryptTo
```
Note: grant is per-key (per-replica). Also need kms:DescribeKey and kms:GetKeyPolicy perms.
chris_sre: Also watch for alias mapping: alias/aws/replica MRK doesnt auto-map in our config; ensure app's config resolves to correct regional ARN.
kms-bot: Reminder: cross-account grants expire on principal deletion. Use least privilege and audit. :rotating_light:
eva_security: TL;DR: MRKs work for regional failover + cross-account if you: (1) replicate MRKs, (2) create per-replica grants/policies for cross-account roles, (3) keep key states healthy, (4) re-encrypt DEKs as part of failover if app can't resolve original key id.
jenna_prodsec: Awesome, thanks. I'll draft runbook steps and a quick test plan. Anyone want to add a quick test case?
chris_sre: Add test: encrypt DEK in us-east-1 primary, attempt decrypt in eu-west-1 replica with and without grant. Document behavior.
raj_infra: I'll add CLI steps to the runbook.
jenna_prodsec: Great, assigning follow-ups: @raj_infra runbook, @chris_sre test plan, @eva_security compliance check. :thumbsup:
